description: Acer pseudoplatanus (sycamore maple), the main host of tar spot; also Norway maple.

diseases.name: Tar Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf disease of maples that leaves raised black spots like drops of tar.
diseases.causes: Spores from last year's fallen leaves are released in spring and infect the new leaves in wet weather.
symptoms: Yellow-green spots appear in early summer
Raised, glossy black 'tar' spots, 1-2 cm, form in late summer
A yellow margin round the spots; some early leaf drop
diseases.effect: Mostly cosmetic; trees are rarely harmed.
diseases.untreated: Heavy years cause some early leaf fall.

steps.title: Rake up fallen leaves
steps.instruction: Collect and compost or remove leaves in autumn.

steps.title: Keep the tree vigorous
steps.instruction: Water in drought and mulch the root area.

steps.title: No spraying needed
steps.instruction: Fungicides are not normally needed for tar spot.
steps.rationale: The disease does not threaten the tree.

lifecycle: The fungus overwinters in fallen leaves.
In spring, spores infect new leaves.
Black tar spots form and fall with the leaves.
conditions: Fallen leaves left under the tree.
